name: add_mcp_server
description:
Add an MCP server to the configuration (tools.mcp.servers). The server is saved to config.json, a connection is attempted immediately, and the result reports live connection status and tool count. Every key in env is stored in the encrypted credential store and referenced from config.json by a ref (mcp_<name>_<key>) — never written in plaintext, mirroring configure_channel's credential handling. sse/http URLs must be https, or http only for loopback addresses (localhost, 127.x.x.x, ::1). Adding a server when MCP is globally disabled and no other server is enabled will turn tools.mcp.enabled ON — an install-wide change; if another server is already enabled the global flag is left alone and the new server will not connect until an operator enables it. A name that already exists is refused, not updated — remove it first with remove_mcp_server. Tools the server exposes register with no tool policy and cannot be called until an operator assigns one. expected_revision must be "absent" (the name's revision from list_mcp_servers); the write is refused if a server of that name appeared since.
Parameters: name (required), expected_revision (required), transport (stdio/sse/http; default stdio), command (required for stdio), url (required for sse/http), args, env.

name: configure_channel
description:
Store a channel's credentials and settings. Secrets (token, app_secret) go into the encrypted credential store and are referenced from config.json by a *_ref — they are never written to config.json in plaintext. Non-secret fields (bot_id, app_id, mode) are written to config.json directly. This does NOT enable the channel and does NOT check whether it is enabled: call enable_channel separately, and note the channel only connects on the next config reload. WhatsApp does not take credentials here — it pairs by QR code in the Channels screen. expected_revision is the channel's revision from list_channels; the write is refused if the channel changed since.
Parameters: id (required, from list_channels), expected_revision (required), token, app_secret, bot_id, app_id, mode.

name: configure_provider
description:
Store an LLM provider's API key in the encrypted credential store and wire it into config.json so the provider becomes usable, then check the SAVED entry: the configured endpoint is asked for its model list over the provider's protocol with the saved credential (local providers need no key). The result's outcome says whether that check passed; it does not prove that a chosen model runs. name must be a catalog provider id (list_models or the Settings → Providers screen show the valid ids; note the ids are 'amazon-bedrock' and 'google', not 'bedrock' or 'gemini'). api_key is required for every cloud provider and optional only for local ones (ollama, lmstudio, vllm). api_base is optional and overrides the catalog's default endpoint; it must be a full http:// or https:// URL with a host. expected_revision is the provider's revision from list_providers ("absent" when it is not configured yet); the write is refused if the provider changed since. dry_run checks the input shape only and saves nothing.
Parameters: name (required), api_key, api_base, expected_revision (required unless dry_run), dry_run.

name: create_agent
description: Create a new agent with personality, model, tools, and configuration. Use agent_type to choose the runtime: 'Main' (default, native chat colleague) and 'Subagent' (native delegation-only worker) require soul; 'subagent_3p' is a delegation-only worker on an external CLI — it takes no soul, requires cli, and its cli_path is optional (empty means the CLI's default binary on PATH). name, description and model are required; soul is required for native agents ('Main'/'Subagent') and must be omitted for 'subagent_3p' (an external CLI worker has no soul; supplying one is refused). A set cli_path must name an executable file this machine can run for the current user (an existing regular file with execute access on Unix; a PATHEXT-admitted extension on Windows); leave it empty to use the CLI's default binary on PATH. color is optional (a palette hex, e.g. #6E8BA8; default Pewter #8E9196) — a color outside the palette is rejected. A new agent created inside a workspace's turn context joins that workspace's core_team when membership succeeds; created with no workspace context it is metadata-only (a member of no team) and cannot run in chat or be delegated to until an operator adds it to a workspace's Team tab — the response's status field (joined_workspace vs metadata_only) reports membership, persistence_status reports durable-save completion (complete, partial, or none), and activation_status reports live publication (active, failed, or not_attempted); joined_workspace alone does not prove the agent is live or runnable — check persistence_status, activation_status and any publish_warning before reporting it ready.

name: create_skill
description: Author a NEW skill (procedural memory). Writes a SKILL.md to the user skills directory; prior versions are snapshotted for rollback. This call writes the file; it is not a confirmation step. Policy may still Ask at execution; that is not a substitute for the user's confirmation of the proposal, and you must not invent a second confirmation ritual. content must not exceed 262144 bytes. A name that already exists is refused — use edit_skill to modify it instead. Parameters: name (required, alphanumeric+hyphens), content (required, full SKILL.md including YAML frontmatter with name and description).

name: create_workspace
description:
Create a new workspace to group related tasks. Call this when the user mentions starting a new workspace, initiative, or area of work. Returns the created workspace's id — pass this id as workspace_id to create_task when delivering tasks to the workspace. Members named in core_team also get the default delegation trust edges between them, so they can delegate to each other immediately. name is capped at 200 characters and description at 2000; exceeding either is rejected.
Parameters: name (required, workspace title), description (optional, free text), core_team (optional, list of agent IDs associated with this workspace).

name: delete_agent
description:
Delete an agent. IRREVERSIBLE. Removes the agent's entity record and applicable SOUL.md instructions. Preserves unrelated files in its home, including HEARTBEAT.md, local skills, and any vestigial MEMORY.md left by an older install. Also cascades: every chat session in the shared session store that belongs SOLELY to this agent is deleted, together with its uploaded files — a session another agent also participated in (e.g. via a mid-conversation agent switch) is left untouched to avoid destroying that agent's history, and is reported separately in the response. Every GTD task assigned to this agent is unassigned (not deleted — the task itself survives); tasks it merely created keep that historical attribution. This agent is also removed from every workspace's core_team, and every delegation-trust edge naming it (as either side) is dropped from each affected workspace's delegation graph. Seeded built-ins (Mia, Jim, Omnipus, Planner, Researcher, General Purpose, Judge, and Plan Supervisor) cannot be deleted. An agent that owns at least one active (running) Plan cannot be deleted — stop/reassign the Plan(s) before retrying. A step that fails partway through is reported in the response rather than silently swallowed — check for a warning field before assuming the cascade fully completed.
Parameters: id (required), revision (required, from get_agent), confirm (bool, must be true).

name: delete_workspace
description: Delete a workspace. This is IRREVERSIBLE and destroys more than the workspace record: its GTD tasks, mount grants, delegation graph, and workspace directory are permanently removed; workflow-status tasks that still reference it become orphans. Read it with get_workspace first. Parameters: id, revision from that read, and confirm:true are all required.

name: disable_channel
description:
Disable a channel connection. The channel will stop on the next config reload. A channel that has never been configured cannot be disabled — it is already inactive. expected_revision is the channel's revision from list_channels; the write is refused if the channel changed since.
Parameters: id (required, the channel type e.g. 'telegram', 'discord'), expected_revision (required).

name: edit_skill
description: Edit / refine an EXISTING skill (self-improvement). Snapshots the prior version for rollback, then writes the new SKILL.md. This call writes the file; it is not a confirmation step. Policy may still Ask at execution; that is not a substitute for the user's confirmation of the proposal, and you must not invent a second confirmation ritual. Editing a built-in creates a user override; the built-in is never mutated in place. content must not exceed 262144 bytes. Parameters: name, content (full new SKILL.md), and revision from the reviewed skill read are required. A conflict means the skill changed after review; stop, reread, and do not retry the stale write.

name: enable_channel
description:
Enable a channel connection. The channel will start on the next config reload. Call list_channels for valid ids. Enabling a channel with no credentials configured is allowed but the channel will fail to connect — configure it with configure_channel first. expected_revision is the channel's revision from list_channels; the write is refused if the channel changed since.
Parameters: id (required, the channel type e.g. 'telegram', 'discord'), expected_revision (required).

name: get_agent
description: Read one agent's sanitized configuration, instructions, editable fields, stored assignments, revision, and activation status. Use get_agent_tools for the full tool catalog.

name: get_agent_tools
description: List tools and effective policies. For an existing agent or new-agent preview, allow/ask lines show name, effective policy, and a description of at most 40 characters; deny lines show only name and deny. Previews use main or worker defaults. ToolSearch reports allow. Existing agents use the effective policy, not only the stored override.

name: get_config
description:
Read a setting (port, timeout, host, feature flag, or similar) from config.json by dot-notation key, e.g. 'gateway.port', 'sandbox.mode'. Pair with set_config to change a value. Credential-shaped fields (API keys, secrets, tokens, passwords) and a handful of security-critical keys (gateway account/token data, the whole sandbox namespace's writable form, etc.) are refused or returned redacted — use list_providers to check configured providers without exposing keys.
Parameters: key (required, e.g. 'gateway.port').

name: get_usage
description:
Query token usage by period, agent, model, or session.
Parameters:
  period   — time window: day, week, month (default), or all
  by       — grouping dimension: agent (default), model, or session
  agent_id — optional: restrict to a single agent
  session_id — optional: restrict to a single session
Returns input, output, cache-read, cache-write, and total token counts.
No dollar amounts — token counts only.
External CLI subagents (subagent_3p) run on a separate engine and are excluded.
If some sessions could not be read the response sets partial=true with partial_error_count — treat the totals as a lower bound in that case.

name: get_workspace
description:
Get a workspace by ID, including its authoritative team, delegation graph, revision, and live task count.
Use this before every workspace mutation and for readback. Returns id, name, description, status, pinned, pin_order, is_default, core_team, delegation, revision, task_count, created_at, and updated_at.
Parameters: id (required, from list_workspaces).

name: list_channels
description: List every messaging channel Omnipus supports — Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, Slack, Matrix, Google Chat, IRC, LINE, Feishu, QQ, DingTalk, WeCom, Weixin — with each one's live state: not_configured, needs_credentials, or configured, plus whether it is currently enabled. Use the returned id with enable_channel, configure_channel, or test_channel. No parameters required.

name: list_mcp_servers
description: List all MCP servers configured in tools.mcp.servers with their transport, enabled state, and live connection status (connected/error/disconnected, from the same live readback add_mcp_server uses). Environment variables are never returned — they may hold credential-store references or, for servers configured before that mechanism existed, real secrets. No parameters required.

name: list_models
description:
List models actually available from your configured providers. This queries each provider's live /models API (up to 15s per provider), so it doubles as a real connectivity and credential check — it is what test_provider points you to. Returns each model's slug, its provider, and whether it is the system default, plus the configured default_model. Providers that have no API key, no known base URL, or that fail to respond are omitted from the list and reported in `warnings` — check that field before treating the list as complete.
Parameters: provider (optional, filter to one provider).

name: list_providers
description: List the providers configured in config.json and whether each one has an API key present in the credential store (key_present / no_credentials). API keys are never returned, and no network call is made — key_present means a key is stored, not that it works. Use list_models to exercise a provider's live API. No parameters required.

name: list_skills
description: List installed skills. scope=usable (the default) lists only skills assigned for this agent to run. scope=management lists sanitized installed inventory for configuration review when the caller has management-read authority; name may inspect one skill's sanitized content in management scope. Use Skill to run an assigned skill and find_skills to search the marketplace.

name: list_workspaces
description:
List workspaces with their live task counts. Call this to find workspace ids to use with create_task, list_tasks (their optional workspace_id), get_workspace, or update_workspace. Ordering is: the default workspace first, then pinned workspaces by pin_order, then the rest newest-first — so the first result is not necessarily the most recently created one. Returns id, name, description, status, pinned, pin_order, is_default, core_team and task_count. Any workspace file that cannot be read is skipped and counted in `skipped`.
Parameters: status (optional: active/archived/all, defaults to active).

name: read_agent_metadata
description: Read one of an agent's three metadata files: SOUL.md (personality, persona, system prompt and behavioural instructions), HEARTBEAT.md (proactive schedule), or AGENT.md (frontmatter config). Defaults to the calling agent's own files; pass agent_id to read another agent's. There is no per-target permission check — any agent granted this tool can read any agent's metadata. Use recall_memory to access memories.

name: remove_mcp_server
description:
Remove an MCP server from the configuration (tools.mcp.servers) and persist the change. expected_revision is the server's revision from list_mcp_servers; the removal is refused if the server changed since.
Parameters: name (required), confirm (bool, must be true), expected_revision (required).

name: remove_skill
description: Remove a project or installation-wide skill. IRREVERSIBLE — the skill's whole directory, including any version history it holds, is permanently deleted; there is no undo. It searches the target workspace's project shelf first and removes a matching skill from its own project. Only if no project skill matches does it use the installation's skills directory, which also contains installation-wide authored skills and user overrides. A project-shelf read failure returns READ_FAILED without removal or fallback; project-path integrity errors also stop removal instead of falling back. A skill present only on the built-in shelf is not removed. If the removed skill was shadowing a lower-priority skill of the same id (an override or a built-in), that one becomes visible again. Parameters: name (required, the skill id as reported by list_skills — no path separators), revision (required from the reviewed skill read), confirm (bool, must be true). A conflict requires a fresh read; do not retry the stale deletion.

name: run_doctor
description: Run a narrow set of security diagnostic checks (exec egress config, credentials.json/config.json file permissions, audit log directory presence) and return checks_failed_pct — the percentage of THESE FEW checks that failed — plus actionable recommendations. This is NOT a comprehensive security audit: it never looks at sandbox.mode, god-mode, dev_mode_bypass, or Landlock/seccomp availability, so an install with every real protection disabled can still score 0% ("no risk"). A low checks_failed_pct means only these specific checks passed, not that the install is secure. No parameters required.

name: set_agent_permissions
description: Change an existing agent's per-agent tool policies and connector (MCP) assignments. This is the only agent-tool path for those changes — update_agent refuses both. The shipped policy asks the user for approval before it runs; Omnipus skips approvals in God Mode. Send id, revision (the opaque revision returned by get_agent), and at least one of tool_policy_changes or mcp_servers. A stale revision or any other input field is refused; re-read the agent before retrying a stale write. tool_policy_changes is a sparse patch: set maps tool names to allow|ask|deny, and remove lists per-agent override names to delete. Unknown tools and invalid policy values are rejected; per-agent policies cannot widen the global tool policy. mcp_servers replaces the full connector-assignment list; [] clears all bindings. Each entry is {id, tools?}: omitted tools grants all tools of that assigned server, an empty tools list grants none. Unknown servers or unknown/unavailable tool names are rejected. External CLI workers reject these capability fields; Judge and Plan Supervisor keep fixed capabilities. Omnipus refuses any per-agent ask as a whole — use deny, or set ask on the global tool policy.

name: set_config
description:
Update a setting (port, timeout, host, feature flag, or similar) in config.json by dot-notation key, e.g. 'gateway.port', 'sandbox.tool_policies'. Only updates settings that already exist — it never creates a new one, and a key naming nothing that exists is refused rather than silently dropped. Writable sections are limited to: gateway., agents., sandbox., channels., tools., providers, workspace_path — everything else is refused. Within those, several security-critical subtrees are refused too, even though their prefix is writable: the whole sandbox.* namespace, gateway.dev_mode_bypass/users/token/cli_token/public_url/trust_xff, tools.exec/mcp/browser/allow_read_paths/allow_write_paths, and the channel ownership fields channels.*.identity/workspace_id — each refusal names where the setting actually belongs. Credential/API-key-shaped values (api_key, secret, token, password in the name) are always refused here — use configure_provider or configure_channel instead, which route secrets into the encrypted credential store. The result includes a requires_restart field: when true, the change was saved but has no effect until the operator restarts the gateway — check it and relay that to the user rather than assuming the change is already live.
Parameters: key (required), value (required).

name: test_channel
description:
Check a channel's stored configuration: that the channel type is known, that a config entry exists, whether it is enabled, and whether credentials are present. Does NOT contact the platform — this makes zero network calls, so a revoked or wrong token still reports success=true, and a channel that is configured but disabled also reports success=true (read the `enabled` field). Enable it with enable_channel and watch the gateway log for the real connection result.
Parameters: id (required, from list_channels).

name: test_provider
description:
Check that this provider's API key resolves in the credential store.
Does NOT contact the provider — this makes zero network calls, so a revoked, expired, or wrong API key can still report status="ok" here. Local providers (ollama, lmstudio, vllm) always report ok — they need no key. A failed check comes back as a normal result with status="error", not as a tool error. Parameters: name (required). Use list_models to actually exercise the connection against the provider's live API.

name: update_agent
description: Update an existing agent using the revision returned by get_agent. Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is. Mia, Jim, Omnipus, Planner, Researcher, and General Purpose keep their built-in identity and instructions, while their skills are editable. An existing agent's per-agent tool policies and connector (MCP) assignments are changed with set_agent_permissions, never update_agent. Judge and Plan Supervisor allow instruction and supported tuning changes but keep fixed tool, connector, and skill capabilities. An empty provider clears its pin. Use fallback_models with model/provider objects; [] clears the fallback chain. The agent type and an external agent's cli/cli_path cannot change after creation; create a new agent for a different type.

name: update_workspace
description: Update an existing workspace using the revision returned by get_workspace. Call this to change its name, description, status, pin state, complete core team, or complete delegation graph. Omitted fields are preserved. core_team replaces the entire team. Omitted delegation preserves valid existing edges, removes edges for removed members, and may seed approved edges for newly added built-ins; an explicit delegation array replaces the graph for continuing members, and [] clears their lines; each member newly added by the same update still receives its self-line unless the operator's seed defaults exclude it. Read the workspace first, include all intended membership and graph effects in the proposal, then submit its id and revision.
